claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside it inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends structuring Git repositories for publishing packages as described, and following these practices improves reliability, maintainability, and delivery speed.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository, and its version is the Git tag on that repository.
Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow: apply a semver Git tag, then run `pulumi package publish`, typically from a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
`pulumi package publish` sends package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.

Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry; source-based packages referenced directly from a Pulumi.yaml file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), even if not a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
The version of an executable-based package is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can publish executable-based packages to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
A repository containing multiple Pulumi packages must either release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that conflicts with how Pulumi consumes packages.
Pulumi recommends exactly one Pulumi package per repository, regardless of package type.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
A single PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.
Bundling unrelated components into one package versions every component identically on each release, which violates semver; Pulumi does not recommend a single monorepo with one giant package.
The Publishing packages guide exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/publishing-packages/.
